title: The shape after a chain of movement ops
starter:
type op = Reshape of int list | Permute of int list | Pad of int list | Expand of int list | Reduce of int

(* the shape after applying ops in order; the inputs are always valid *)
let rec shape_after (shape : int list) (ops : op list) : int list =
  shape
hints: Recurse over the list: work out the shape after the first op, then carry on with the rest.
Reshape and Expand name the new shape outright. Permute picks `List.nth shape p` for each p in the order. Pad adds a left and a right amount to each axis.
Reduce m drops the first m axes: `List.filteri (fun i _ -> i >= m) shape`.

answer.code:
type op = Reshape of int list | Permute of int list | Pad of int list | Expand of int list | Reduce of int

let rec shape_after (shape : int list) (ops : op list) : int list =
  match ops with
  | [] -> shape
  | op :: rest ->
    let s = match op with
      | Reshape s | Expand s -> s
      | Permute order -> List.map (fun p -> List.nth shape p) order
      | Pad pads -> List.mapi (fun k d -> d + List.nth pads (2 * k) + List.nth pads (2 * k + 1)) shape
      | Reduce m -> List.filteri (fun i _ -> i >= m) shape
    in
    shape_after s rest
answer.explain: Movement ops never look at the data, so a shape is enough to type check a whole chain. Each op is a small function of the old shape, and folding them left to right gives the final one.
